name: Busana kerawang Gayo
note: Gayo clothing decorated with distinctive kerawang embroidery.

name: Ayam betutu
note: This Balinese chicken dish is seasoned with a rich spice mixture and slowly cooked.

name: Tradisi Nganggung
note: Bangka families bring food on covered trays to share at communal gatherings.

name: Tradisi Tabot
note: Bengkulu’s Tabot observance commemorates Husayn through rituals in the month of Muharram.

name: Angeun lada
note: This spicy meat soup is found in southern Banten, including Pandeglang and Lebak.

name: Tari Saronde
note: The wedding ritual Molapi saronde uses a scarf in a dance led by the groom.

name: Tari Sekapur Sirih
note: Dancers welcome guests while carrying a ceremonial betel offering.

name: Wayang golek
note: Sundanese wooden-puppet theatre blends storytelling, music, humor and moral lessons.

name: Soto Betawi
note: A Jakarta beef soup with a creamy broth made with coconut milk, milk or both.

name: Telok Belanga
note: Malay men in West Kalimantan wear this attire for weddings and customary occasions.

name: Busana manik-manik Dayak Kenyah
note: Beaded patterns decorate Kenyah ta’a and sapei sapaq attire, traditions also found in North Kalimantan.

name: Baju kurung Melayu
note: Malay communities in the Riau Islands wear this loose, modest traditional garment.

name: Joget Dangkong
note: This Malay social dance is performed in communities across the Riau Islands.

name: Kerajinan kain Sasirangan
note: Banjar artisans create patterned cloth using running stitches and resist-dyeing techniques.

name: Tradisi kematian Tiwah
note: This sacred Kaharingan mortuary ceremony guides the deceased’s spirit and is not merely a performance.

name: Tari Jugit
note: Women perform this graceful classical dance to honour guests and mark customary occasions.

name: Tari Melinting
note: This East Lampung dance is historically linked to the Melinting court.

name: Tifa totobuang
note: Maluku musicians combine tifa drums with rows of small totobuang gongs.

name: Tari Tide-Tide
note: Men and women perform this social dance at celebrations in North Halmahera.

name: Gendang beleq
note: This Sasak ensemble in Lombok combines large drums with music and coordinated movement.

name: Sasando
note: This plucked string instrument from Rote uses a lontar-leaf resonator around a bamboo body.

name: Tari Isolo (Sentani)
note: Also called Isosolo, this communal dance is performed on boats on Lake Sentani.

name: Ikan bakar Manokwari
note: Fresh grilled fish is topped with a lively chilli, shallot and lime sambal.

name: Tambelo
note: Kamoro communities gather tambelo molluscs from mangrove wood as a local food.

name: Zapin Meskom
note: This local zapin tradition comes from Meskom in Bengkalis.

name: Upacara Tulude (Sangihe)
note: Sangihe communities give thanks together through the annual Tulude ceremony.

name: Tari Piring
note: Minangkabau dancers move rhythmically while holding plates in their hands.

name: Kabuto
note: A traditional cassava food found in Muna culinary traditions.

name: Pallubasa
note: A Makassar meat soup enriched with toasted grated coconut.

name: Bau peapi
note: A Mandar fish dish often eaten with jepa.

name: Tekwan
note: Small fish-and-tapioca dumplings are served in a savory shrimp broth.

name: Uta kelo
note: This Kaili dish cooks moringa leaves in seasoned coconut milk.

name: Bika ambon
note: Despite its name, this honeycombed cake is associated with Medan.
